incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — Observed sharp degradation in cache hit-rate for prefix/KV layer in us-west-2 starting ~2026-03-15T03:02:00Z. Auto-paging on-call. Impact: higher tail latency for text-generation, increased token cost for affected tenants. Paging group: infra-oncall.

Sanjay K: acked. On-call ramping up, pulling dashboards now. Visible spike in 503s for a few customers? digging.

Sanjay K: quick note — alert rule: `kv.prefix_hitrate < 0.2` triggered across multiple hosts (all backends in pool-3).

Alex W: adding context — we merged runtime change `runtime-v2.17` 03:01 UTC that adjusted eviction behavior for prefix caches (opt-in flag `prefix_invalidation_mode=eager`). Could be related.

Alex W: logs from one host (tail):
```
2026-03-15T03:02:12Z host-az1 instance-17 INFO kv_cache: prefix_lookup miss=0.87 hit=0.13 total=124312
2026-03-15T03:02:12Z host-az1 instance-17 WARN cache: eviction_rate=892/sec policy=eager
2026-03-15T03:02:13Z host-az2 instance-04 INFO requests: gen_latency_p95=1.86s gen_errors=0.6%
```

Priya D: pulling traces now — instrumented prefix lookup spans available. Correlating with deploy id.

Morgan L: stepping in for handoff (on-call overlap). I'm going to coordinate mitigations: 1) revert or toggle back `prefix_invalidation_mode` to `lazy` on a small subset; 2) temporarily increase prefix TTL on affected hosts; 3) enable warming job to pre-populate hot prefixes.

Sanjay K: mitigation step 1 executed on canary (hosts host-az1a, host-az1b) — toggled `prefix_invalidation_mode=lazy` via admin API. Confirming metrics.

Zeus (ops-bot): deploy-api: PATCH /admin/cache/config -> 200 OK (runtime-v2.17, change-id c897b2)

Alex W: metric update after toggle (1m window): `kv.prefix_hitrate` improved on canary from 0.12 -> 0.48, request latency p95 reduced ~40%. Not full recovery yet.

Emily R: customer impact note — flagged 3 paying customers with elevated latency; reached out via account owners. No data exfiltration, just degraded performance and cost spike.

Priya D: pulled span sample: majority of misses are for short prefix lookups (<= 64 tokens) and show cold KV misses triggered by high eviction churn. Exporting sample traces to #eng-telemetry.

Alex W: quick query I ran on logs-index:
```sql
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) AS t, avg(prefix_hitrate) as hr, sum(evictions) as ev FROM cache_metrics WHERE cluster='us-west-2' AND ts > '2026-03-15T02:45:00Z' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t;
```
Result: hr bottomed at 0.11 at 03:03, evictions peaked 890/s.

Morgan L: mitigation step 2: increased `prefix_ttl` from 300 -> 3600 on affected pool via admin API. Command: `curl -X POST https://svc-admin/cache -d '{"prefix_ttl":3600}'` (rolled to pool-3).

Alex W: warming job scheduled — spin up async job to re-populate top-500 prefixes per tenant for 15m window. `jobs.trigger('prefix-warm', tenants=[...])` started.

Zeus (ops-bot): job-runner: started job prefix-warm job-id=pw-20260315-001 on pool-3.

Priya D: traces show warming job hitting the same prefix keys; second-order effect — slight bump in write op counts but reads recover.

Sanjay K: system note — rollback of `runtime-v2.17` flagged as option. We did targeted toggle but not full rollback yet. Need to decide during post-incident review.

Emily R: assembling initial incident summary for customers and execs: impact window 03:02 — ongoing mitigation; primary cause suspected config change during runtime-v2.17 deploy that increased eviction aggressiveness (eager invalidation) interacting with recent increase in short-tail traffic.

Alex W: hypothesis tracking (in-thread):
- H1: recent deploy changed invalidation mode -> immediate eviction churn -> low prefix hit-rate. Evidence: deploy time correlation + config flag. (Status: supported by canary metric changes)
- H2: unrelated memory pressure on hosts causing evictions (swap/oom). Evidence: no OOM logs on hosts, memory usage normal. (Status: weak)
- H3: upstream client behaviour changed causing many unique prefix keys (bad prompts). Evidence: request sample shows increased unique prefix entropy but not enough to explain magnitude. (Status: partial)

Morgan L: immediate action items (assigned):
- Alex W: gather full deploy rollout map and flag list for v2.17 (due +30m).
- Priya D: export representative spans and sample keys to S3 for offline RCA (+60m).
- Sanjay K: monitor and hold mitigation config for 2h, watch hit-rate and latency.
- Emily R: draft customer impact comms and postmortem template.

Sanjay K: update at 03:35Z — metrics stabilizing on canary, cluster-level still improving but not fully recovered. Will keep monitoring.

Emily R: note for postmortem — include timeline, config diff, and warm-up coverage; recommend adding canary checks for prefix_hitrate on deploys.

Alex W: pushed a short log bundle to /incidents/1782501234/logs.tar.gz and a config diff at https://internal.redwood/reports/1782501234/config-diff.

Morgan L: handoff plan — I'm taking shift until 07:00Z. If anything regresses, page infra-oncall. We'll collect artifacts and do a full RCA doc later.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigations applied, partial recovery observed. Keep thread updated.

Emily R: closing note for thread: please add any additional observations or evidence here (screenshots, query IDs, trace IDs). We'll convert to postmortem doc once the metrics fully stabilize. :white_check_mark:
